The written story of a person's life — Biografía.
He wrote a biography of Churchill.
Plural: biographies. If you write your own it is an autobiography.
Make something completely wet — Empapar / calar.
The rain drenched us in seconds.
A large group of insects moving together — Enjambre.
A swarm of bees passed over the garden.
Move in a large crowd — Pulular / arremolinarse.
v|Phrase: swarming with, meaning full of.
Move unsteadily from side to side — Tambalearse / bambolearse.
The table wobbles on this floor.
Loud confused noise from a crowd — Tumulto / alboroto.
Sad and without hope — Abatido/a / desanimado/a.
Noun: dejection. Verb: deject, now rare.
Doing what you are told — Obediente.
Verb: obey. Noun: obedience. Opposite: disobedient.
Move back or away — Retroceder / retirarse.
Become weaker or further off — Desvanecerse / alejarse.
A cruel ruler with total power — Tirano/a / déspota.
Noun: tyranny. Note the pronunciation: TY-rant.
An organisation that helps people in need — Organización benéfica / entidad de caridad.
She works for a children's charity.
Giving money or help to the poor — Caridad / beneficencia.
Kindness in judging others — Indulgencia / caridad.
Show a little charity towards him.
The decision of a jury or judge — Veredicto / fallo.
The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
An opinion or judgement — Veredicto / opinión.
What is your verdict on the film?
Dig something out of the ground — Desenterrar.
Discover something hidden — Sacar a la luz / descubrir.
Leave, especially on a journey — Partir / salir.
Do something differently from usual — Apartarse de.
He departed from the written speech.
Happen at the same time — Coincidir.
Be the same; agree — Coincidir / concordar.
Say that a planned thing will not happen — Cancelar / anular.
Cross something out so it cannot be used — Anular / inutilizar.
v|Noun: cancellation. British English doubles the l: cancelled.
The debtor agreed to pay monthly.
The b is silent, as in debt. Opposite: creditor.
Opposite: illegible. Careful: legible is about writing, eligible means qualified.
A large printed notice or sign — Pancarta / cartel.
Often held up at a demonstration.
Spreading from person to person by contact — Contagioso/a.
Spreading easily to others, of feelings — Contagioso/a.
Priests and ministers as a group — Clero.
Takes a plural verb. One person is a member of the clergy or a clergyman.
Usual; done by custom — Acostumbrado/a / habitual.
It is customary to tip the waiter.
The box has a transparent lid.
Easy to understand; open — Transparente / claro/a.
Burn with hot liquid or steam — Escaldar / quemar con líquido.
He scalded his hand with the kettle.
Heat a liquid almost to boiling — Escalfar / calentar casi hasta hervir.
Scald the milk before adding it.
v|Careful: scald is with liquid, burn is with fire.
A disease that spreads quickly to many people — Epidemia.
The flu epidemic closed the schools.
A sudden rise in something bad — Epidemia / oleada.
There is an epidemic of car thefts.
A worldwide one is a pandemic.
The condition of being very overweight — Obesidad.
Obesity raises the risk of diabetes.
Make something look larger — Ampliar / aumentar.
The lens magnifies the image ten times.
Make something seem more important than it is — Exagerar / magnificar.
Person who treats pain by adjusting the spine — Quiropráctico/a.
The chiropractor worked on his back.
The ch sounds like k. The treatment is chiropractic.
Something that blocks the way — Obstáculo.
A fallen tree was the only obstacle.
Something that makes progress difficult — Obstáculo / impedimento.
Lack of money is the main obstacle.
Let fresh air into a room — Ventilar / airear.
Open a window to ventilate the kitchen.
The issue was ventilated at the meeting.
The change had a negative effect.
The temperature was negative all day.
Regular money paid to someone who has retired — Pensión / jubilación.
He lives on a small pension.
A person receiving one is a pensioner.
Belonging to a city or town — Municipal.
The municipal swimming pool is free.
We have an oral exam on Friday.
Adverb: orally. Careful: oral sounds almost like aural, which means of the ear.
